economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00052227492: Two-pass public-evidence and corrective gap-closure audit for Flexential's Minneapolis-Chaska data center on parcel 30.0590020 at 3500 Lyman Boulevard. The review covered Carver County parcel, valuation-notice, tax-statement and payment records; City of Chaska permit, inspection, agenda, archive, budget, utility and annual-financial-report sources; Minnesota DEED, Revenue, statutory, environmental, workforce and utility-regulatory sources; federal environmental, workplace-safety and county-economic access points; current and archived operator, predecessor, career and ESG materials; contractor and supplier references; and education, workforce and recipient-reported community sources for 2013-2026. Twenty-three quantitative observations are preserved: a source-projected original investment lower bound; three later non-cumulative permit values; current floor area and critical-load UPS capacity; three annual parcel-tax payments; one current parcel-tax bill; five exact-parcel taxable-market-value stocks for payable 2023-2027; and eight historical Via West Inc. estimated-actual-value observations. The exact parcel statements crosswalk the 2023-2025 city-table values to parcel 30.0590020, but the duplicate value concepts are alternative assessor presentations and are not additive. Stream's facilities at 1706 and 1708 West Creek Lane, the IP Stream Minneapolis LLC development agreement and its municipal rebates are outside the selected 3500 Lyman Boulevard project boundary and are not duplicated in this fragment; the six base Stream rebate rows require reassignment or removal from this target by the orchestrator because project fragments are append-only. Permit values are administrative estimates and are not summed because scopes may overlap. Parcel taxes span all taxing jurisdictions and special assessments, not City-only receipts or net benefit. No synthesis fragment is added because candidate-by-candidate review found no defensible project inputs for construction labor, realized operating employment or payroll, supplier payments, metered energy or water, emissions, facility-specific incentive value, public-service costs, quantified community transfers, or a causal county employment, wage or GDP effect. prj_study_im3_building_00116005354: Two-pass project-scoped audit of Apple Maiden under worker-research-contract 2.0.0. The governed project is IM3 building 00116005354, a 564,402-square-foot mapped roof footprint within Apple's larger 5977 Startown Road campus; every economic observation remains campus- or company/county-unallocated because public records do not allocate it to that building. The original facility is kept distinct from the 2012 tactical/fuel-cell work, the 2022 MDN.06 237,600-square-foot building and the capacity expansion under construction in 2025. Reported actuals, original commitments, permit valuations and contextual operating facts remain separate, and the post-search modeling gate retains no estimates. prj_study_im3_building_00172739953: Corrective public-evidence and candidate-modeling audit for Switch Las Vegas NAP7, the individual real-property parcel and original SUPERNAP building at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard. The review covered Clark County assessor and ownership history, Treasurer, Accela permits, rights-of-way, planning, air quality, budgets and financial reports; Nevada incentive, tax and utility-regulatory sources; operator, SEC, workforce, supplier and contractor materials; and recipient-reported community records for 2005-2026. Six direct observations remain after the corrective pass; no wider Core Campus capital expenditure, combined incentive audit, later facility, personal property, tenant equipment, vendor equipment, company-wide employment or parcel-transfer price is recast as NAP7 contribution. One modeled synthesis is retained under the last-resort modeling gate: the fiscal-year 2027 real-property bill defines an exactly same-account assessed-liability public-service-cost break-even threshold. It is not actual public cost, collected revenue, jurisdictional receipt or a net fiscal result. Candidate models for investment, construction, suppliers, operations, resources, community benefits, net fiscal effects and county employment, GDP and wages were rejected for missing facility inputs, incompatible scope or timing, overlap, non-identification or lack of decision relevance. NAP7 employment, payroll, local supplier payments, metered electricity and water, personal-property tax, realized abatement, jurisdictional receipts, actual project-attributable public costs and net fiscal impact remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00214321737: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every sourced amount remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records preserve Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; assessor and tax records provide parcel-value stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permits provide discrete administrative values and contractors; MEPA and MassDEP records establish supporting electric work and permit-listed generators; and two recipient records verify separate community contributions. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Source-family gap closure found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility-upgrade cost, annual water or wastewater series, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. One last-resort synthesis survives: the exact FY2026 real-property-bill amount is reused only as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, not as observed cost, collected revenue or a net fiscal result; all other contribution and GDP, employment and wage candidates are rejected individually in the project updates. prj_study_im3_building_00300974499: Corrective two-pass public-evidence audit of Apple Mesa at 3740 S Signal Butte Road. The selected IM3 object is one 1,338,261-square-foot mapped building footprint, while the assessor describes a 1,255,156-square-foot Computer Center improvement and the permit, tax, utility, FTZ and operator sources generally cover the whole converted facility or related supporting infrastructure. The account therefore retains campus, company-county and supporting-infrastructure facts as unallocated unless a source supplies a narrower crosswalk. Twenty-five direct observations are added: the assessor floor-area fact and twenty-four completed positive-valuation Apple-era permits omitted from the prior account. Permit valuations are administrative amounts and related permits or addenda are not summed. All direct tax, payment, investment, electricity, renewable-capacity and projection records already in the base account remain; no unsupported zero is introduced. Direct water use, wastewater volume, utility bills, facility payroll, worker residence, local supplier payments, realized IOC relief, project-attributable community payments, marginal public-service costs and causal county outcomes remain unresolved. prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00388148510: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for TierPoint's Little Rock data center at 15707 Chenal Parkway in Pulaski County, Arkansas. Current operator and assessor records support three separately defined operating-floor-area observations, including a nested raised-floor subset; existing canonical assessor and Treasurer records retain parcel values and one unpaid tax-account amount. Parcel sale prices, portfolio transaction values, headquarters incentives, a void right-of-way permit, equipment ratings, storage-tank registrations and a current vacancy are not relabeled as project investment, construction spending, resource use, employment or public contribution. Gap closure found no site-attributable capital outlay, construction workforce or payroll, supplier payment or local-purchase share, operating headcount or payroll, cash tax receipt or recipient cash distribution, realized incentive, marginal public-service cost, metered annual electricity, water or wastewater, emissions, or recipient-verified community contribution. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Direct investment, realized employment or payroll, supplier payments, community transfers, facility-only resource consumption, incentives, and public-service costs remain unavailable; bounded arithmetic and engineering sensitivities are kept in the separate modeled-synthesis fragment. prj_study_im3_building_00598261190: Corrective public-evidence and last-resort modeling audit for the State Farm data center at 24400 West Valley Parkway in Olathe, Kansas. No site-level employment, payroll, supplier payment, community transfer, metered electricity or water, claimed incentive amount, actual marginal public-service cost, net fiscal position or attributable county effect is inferred from public material. prj_study_im3_building_00626785488: Corrective two-pass public-evidence audit for the individual 654,433-square-foot IM3-mapped building footprint within Meta's Los Lunas data-center campus at 4250 Messenger Loop NW. The search matrix covered original-campus chronology and financing; Village budgets, audits, LEDA, development, planning, permit, traffic, fire, water and wastewater records; Valencia County assessor, treasurer and clerk access; New Mexico economic-development, workforce, court, Construction Industries Division, Public Regulation Commission and Environment Department materials; PNM filings; Meta operator and SEC materials; contractors and suppliers; community recipients; and federal county GDP, employment and wage data through September 6, 2026. Building-level capital expenditure, permits and fees, payroll, resident employment, supplier payments, metered electricity and water, utility bills, tax or PILOT payments, cash value of realized abatements, public-service costs and net fiscal results remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_00838817907: Two-pass contribution-account audit for TierPoint Charlotte Center Park (CL4), the tenant-operated data-center building at 1805 Center Park Drive on Mecklenburg County parcel 14106108. This fragment retains nine building-level observations: opening total and raised-floor area, opening usable UPS capacity, 2020 landlord NLA, 2021 finaled permit value, and current/2024 operator whole-building and raised-floor/production-space measures. It also retains 36 county-context observations from twelve annual County Business Patterns files for NAICS 518210 in 2012-2023; those rows are explicitly county-industry context and cannot establish CL4 employment, payroll or project-level operations completeness. The 36-source total comprises 24 non-CBP substantive sources and twelve annual CBP files. Existing base evidence supplies 42 exact-parcel assessment and tax-bill/payment records for 2013-2026 and is not duplicated in this append-only fragment. Plans, appraisals, transactions, expired/withdrawn/in-progress permits, generic exemptions and unmatched records are not recast as contributions. A separate synthesis fragment retains only minimum one-post continuous-coverage and theoretical opening-electricity sensitivities; original investment, construction labor, suppliers, observed CL4 employment/payroll, personal-property/tenant tax incidence, public costs, metered resources/emissions, community transfers and causal county outcomes remain unresolved. prj_study_im3_building_00844389014: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Google Clarksville in Montgomery County, Tennessee. The review covered Tennessee Comptroller industrial-development-board PILOT filings for 2019-2025; the Montgomery County assessor GIS parcel service and Trustee tax-bill portal; parcel-linked stormwater files; Clarksville-Montgomery County Regional Planning Commission materials; IDB, county-commission and city agenda archives; state and federal environmental portals; operator location, environmental, economic-impact and watershed materials; utility annual reports; and public workforce, contractor, procurement and recipient sources. A single optional synthesis reproduces the operator's 2024 Montgomery County water-consumption identity at unallocated location scope; no multiplier, supplier-retention, fiscal-net, public-cost, energy, payroll or causal county model is created. prj_study_im3_building_00888253616: Second-pass public-evidence audit for NTT Silicon Valley SV1 at 1160 Walsh Avenue, Santa Clara. The selected account is Quicken/Rocket's partial tenancy and data-center use within a landlord-controlled mixed office and data-center property, not the entire combined parcel, separate personal-property accounts, another tenant, the corporate technology workforce, Bedrock's Detroit portfolio, or later third-party utility work. Neither is observed consumption or payroll. Realized total investment, total construction labor, supplier payments and locality, operating employment and payroll, tax bills and payments, project incentive value, public-service costs, metered resources, emissions, community transfers, and a causal county counterfactual remain unresolved. prj_study_im3_building_00978934687: Foundational corrective audit for Digital Crossroad DX-1 at 100 Digital Crossroads Drive, Hammond, Indiana. The selected IM3 building remains the project key, while tax accounts, utility infrastructure, permits, investment, jobs and supplier facts remain at their reported campus, company/county or supporting-infrastructure scopes and are unallocated. Campus, company-county, and supporting-infrastructure observations remain explicitly unallocated to the selected building; later expansion areas and unrelated Eagle Mountain data-center developers are excluded unless a source establishes continuity. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. Most public evidence covers the multi-building Henrico campus or Scout Development's county account and remains unallocated to the selected inventory building; overlapping funding and investment figures are not summed, and unavailable supplier payments, utility bills, tax receipts, incentive costs, payroll, and marginal public-service costs remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_campus_00019988712: Second-pass direct-evidence audit for Meta's Prineville data-center campus at 735 SW Connect Way in Prineville, Crook County. The selected IM3 entity is the campus, not one PRN building, every Vitesse-owned county parcel, Apple's separate campus, or Meta's statewide and global portfolios. The fragment preserves the baseline 2023-2025 Google LLC and Design LLC tax-bill and assessed-value series and the documented $28.5 million water-infrastructure project, and adds only incremental evidence.
